title: Nebius Beats Q3 Revenue Estimates, but Shares Fall 16% on Capex and a Cautious Outlook
dek: Nebius beat revenue estimates in the third quarter, but it set 2027 capex at $40 billion to $45 billion and pointed to the low end of 2026 revenue, and the stock fell 16% on Thursday.
author: Meridian Newsroom

keyPoints: Nebius reported third-quarter revenue of $980.8 million, up 571%, against an LSEG consensus of $907.5 million (Business Wire; CNBC).
Adjusted EBITDA was $465.8 million in the quarter. GAAP net loss from continuing operations was $37.5 million, or 13 cents a share (Business Wire; CNBC).

Shares sank 16% on Thursday, as the revenue beat was overshadowed by the capex plan and the outlook (CNBC).
body:
Nebius Group reported its third-quarter 2026 results before the market opened on Thursday, Nov. 12, and the stock fell sharply despite a revenue beat. The company's earnings webcast was scheduled for 8 a.m. Eastern.

## The quarter

Revenue rose to $980.8 million, a 571% increase from a year earlier, and beat the LSEG consensus of $907.5 million, according to CNBC. Adjusted EBITDA was $465.8 million, and the company reported a net loss from continuing operations of $37.5 million, or 13 cents a share, compared with a loss of $119.6 million a year earlier (Business Wire; CNBC). CNBC noted it was not immediately clear whether the loss per share was comparable to the 69 cents analysts had expected.

The nine-month figures show the scale of the change: revenue of $1.96 billion, up 549%, and adjusted EBITDA of $831.5 million (Business Wire).

## The outlook

The market reacted to the guidance, not the quarter. Management said 2026 revenue would land at the low end of its $3 billion to $3.4 billion range, CNBC reported. That is slightly below the FactSet estimate of $3.35 billion.

Capital spending is the larger issue. Nebius raised its 2026 capex outlook to about $27 billion, from $20 billion to $25 billion, and set an initial 2027 capex range of $40 billion to $45 billion. The FactSet expectation for 2027 was $28.77 billion (CNBC). Revenue guidance for 2027 of $12 billion to $13 billion was close to the $12.09 billion consensus, so the gap is in spending rather than sales.

The company said it raised $5.75 billion in debt financing during the quarter (CNBC). For a company whose spending is rising this fast, financing terms are as important as demand.

## Read-across to the neocloud group

The report came one day after CoreWeave and IREN beat expectations, and Nebius had jumped about 15% on Wednesday on that read-through, CNBC reported. Nvidia, which holds investments across the neocloud group and held about $329 million of Nebius shares at the end of June, according to a filing cited by CNBC, also weighed on the sector during the session. CoreWeave fell 6.4% in an AP midday report, while Micron, a memory supplier to the AI build-out, fell 2.8%.

The stock's reaction is a signal that investors want evidence that heavy spending converts into cash flow at acceptable financing costs. That is the same question the Treasury selloff is asking. With the 10-year yield back above 5%, the cost of that capital is moving the wrong way.

This is analysis, not investment advice. The earnings figures come from Nebius's own release and from CNBC's report on the results.

marketImpact.summary: The revenue beat was overshadowed by a much higher capex plan and a conservative 2026 outlook. Financing costs now matter more for neocloud stocks, and the rate backdrop has moved against them.
marketImpact.timeframe: Thursday, Nov. 12, and the next few sessions as analysts reset targets

tickers.rationale: Shares sank 16% on Thursday after a revenue beat, a 2026 outlook at the low end of guidance and a 2027 capex plan well above expectations (CNBC)
